screening_decisions.reason: Primary case-control study assessing VTE risk in women using low-estrogen combined oral contraceptives. Population includes women without predisposing medical conditions, meeting the criteria for healthy women taking COC with VT as outcome.

Broad epidemiological study evaluating multiple risk factors for VTE (cancer, fractures, surgery, etc.) in the general population. Not focused specifically on healthy women taking COC, and OC use is only one of many risk factors examined.
Interventional trial measuring coagulation parameters (factors V, VII, VIII, etc.) rather than clinical venous thrombosis events. Does not meet the outcome criterion of VT.
Hospital-based case-control study assessing VTE risk in relation to recent oral contraceptive use. Focuses on women with idiopathic DVT/PE, aligning with the criteria.
Case-control study specifically designed to assess VTE risk in nonpredisposed women under 40 using oral contraceptives, directly addressing the selection criteria.
Methodological paper on statistical models for network meta-analysis. Not a clinical study on COC or venous thrombosis.
Review article discussing thrombophilias, OCs, HRT, and IVF. Not a primary research study evaluating VT outcomes in women taking COC.
Primary case-control study investigating the association between oral contraceptive use and venous thromboembolism in women. Meets population, intervention, and outcome criteria.
Consensus statement/survey providing prescription recommendations based on existing literature. Not a primary study.
Review compiling incidence estimates from various studies. Does not present primary data on COC use and VT.
Nested case-control study using GPRD data to compare VTE risk between third- and second-generation combined oral contraceptives. Directly addresses the criteria.
Matched case-control study evaluating VTE risk in women using gestodene-containing OCs versus other progestins. Meets all selection criteria.
Analytical report modeling the relative risk of mortality from venous/pulmonary thromboembolism in US women using oral contraceptives. Relevant to COC and VT outcomes.
Database case-control study comparing VTE risk between second- and third-generation combined oral contraceptives in women aged 18-49. Meets criteria.
Methodological study examining how design decisions (e.g., restricting to hospitalized cases) affect VTE risk estimates in OC studies. Not a primary clinical study.
Describes a cohort and nested case-control study from the UK GPRD assessing VT risk in women using third-generation COCs vs levonorgestrel-containing COCs. Meets criteria.
Large national registry-based cohort study of non-pregnant women with no history of thrombotic disease, assessing VTE risk by progestogen type and estrogen dose. Perfectly matches criteria.
National case-control study estimating the relative risk of fatal pulmonary embolism (a venous thrombotic event) in childbearing-aged women using combined oral contraceptives.
Pharmacovigilance study analyzing adverse event reports for cardiovascular reactions, including venous thrombosis, associated with different COC formulations. Relevant to COC and VT outcomes.
Danish study investigating medical records of young women with confirmed venous thromboembolic disease to assess the association with oral contraceptive use. Meets criteria.
Study includes 65,000 healthy women aged 15-44 assessing oral contraceptive use and venous thromboembolism. Meets all criteria: healthy women population, COC intervention, VT outcome.
Danish case-control study of women 15-44 years old assessing OC influence on VTE risk. Excluded pregnant women and those with previous thrombotic disease. Meets all criteria.
Nested case-control study estimating idiopathic VTE risk in COC users comparing different formulations. Women had no exclusion factors. Meets criteria.
Methodological paper about mixed treatment comparisons illustrated with rheumatoid arthritis drug treatments. No relation to COCs or VTE in women.
Study of women 15-49 without prior VTE, anticoagulants, or hospitalization before OC use. Specifically focuses on young healthy women and VTE risk with different OC generations.
Study includes both men and women, primarily validates APC resistance test. While it analyzes OC-using women as a subgroup, the main focus is test validation, not COC-VTE risk in healthy women.
WHO hospital-based case-control study assessing OC use and VTE/PE risk. Found relative risk of 2.9 for VTE/PE among current/recent OC users. Meets criteria.

Study of reproductive-age women with VTE and healthy controls, examining interaction between OC use and thrombophilic mutations. Includes 140 women with VTE while using OCs and 173 healthy controls on OCs.
Nested case-control study of women 15-39 comparing VTE risk across different OC formulations. Cases were women with well-documented VTE diagnosed in current OC users.
Retrospective study of women 15-44 with fatal VTE coded as cause of death, identifying COC use within 2 months. Compares incidences across different COC types.
Cochrane review comparing contraceptive effectiveness, bleeding patterns, discontinuation, and side effects of different estrogen doses. VTE is not the primary outcome.
Clinical practice guideline for DVT/PE diagnosis. Not a primary research study on COC use and VTE in healthy women.
General epidemiological review of VTE in the US population. Does not focus on COC use or healthy women specifically.
Population-based study of VT incidence and mortality in general Norwegian population aged 20+. Does not focus on COC use.
MEGA case-control study of premenopausal women <50 (not pregnant, not postpartum) assessing VTE risk with different OC types and estrogen doses. Meets all criteria.
Danish national cohort study of women 15-49 with no cardiovascular/malignant disease history. Assesses VTE risk with different hormonal contraceptives including COCs.
Diagnostic accuracy study of clinical model for DVT assessment. No relation to COC use or healthy women population.
Review article describing natural history of VTE/DVT/PE. Does not focus on COC use or healthy women.
Cohort study of women 15-44 in Michigan Medicaid population analyzing VTE risk with different estrogen doses in OCs. Meets all criteria.
Case-control study where minidose oral contraception was identified as main risk factor for DVT in non-menopausal women (OR=6.9). While hospitalized setting, still assesses COC-VTE relationship.

This is a clinical review article, not primary research. Additionally, it covers both hormonal contraceptives AND hormone replacement therapy (HRT), which is outside the scope of COC-specific studies.

Cohort study of women aged 12-50 years using combined oral contraceptives with venous thrombotic events (DVT and PE) as outcomes. Meets all selection criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
This study focuses on lifestyle factors (physical exercise, smoking, alcohol consumption) as exposures for VTE risk, not on COC use. COC use is not the primary intervention being studied.
Uses spontaneous ADR reporting data to estimate VTE incidence in women using different COCs (Yasmin, Cilest, Follimin, Desolett). Studies healthy women on COCs with VT as outcome.
This is a pharmacological review describing progestin structures and properties. No clinical outcomes or patient data presented. Does not study VT outcomes in women taking COCs.

Retrospective analysis of hospitalized adolescents with pulmonary embolism. Population includes both males and females, and focuses on hospitalized patients rather than healthy women on COCs. Not specific to COC users.

Case series of 72 women treated for acute thromboembolic diseases, with 34 using hormonal contraceptives before onset. Studies the link between hormonal contraceptive use and thromboembolic disease in women.
This study focuses on post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) as a complication AFTER DVT, not on VT as the primary outcome. Population includes men and women with established DVT, not healthy women on COCs.

Studies women aged 15-44 with documented thromboembolic events, comparing OC users vs nonusers. While ~25% had congenital thrombophilia, the study includes healthy women and assesses VT risk with OC use. Conservative decision to include.

Nested case-control study of women aged 15-44 using COCs (drospirenone vs levonorgestrel) with non-fatal VTE as outcome. Cases were idiopathic VTE (no identifiable clinical risk factors). Meets selection criteria.
This is a review/commentary article examining epidemiologic studies and discussing controversies. Not primary research with original patient data on healthy women taking COCs with VT outcomes.

This study measures hemostasis variables (surrogate markers) rather than actual venous thrombosis events. Also compares vaginal ring to oral contraceptive, not just COC users. VT is not the outcome measured.

Small study of 28 women with OC-induced venous thrombosis. While 15 had prothrombotic conditions, 13 were normal subjects. Studies age effect on OC-induced VT. Conservative decision to include due to presence of healthy women.

Case-control study investigating interaction between genetic mutations and OC use in DVT. Includes healthy controls and assesses OC use as risk factor. While focused on genetic interactions, it includes healthy women on OCs with VT outcomes.

Case-control study of Thai women with VTE vs healthy controls, examining OC pill use as a risk factor. Controls were healthy women attending gynecological clinic. Meets selection criteria for healthy women and VT outcome.

Abstract is truncated and incomplete. Study focuses on protein C deficiency in healthy blood donors and families with thrombophilia. Does not clearly address COC use with VT outcomes in healthy women.
This is a methodological paper describing supplementary data collection to assess residual confounding in another study. Not primary research on healthy women taking COCs with VT outcomes.

Analysis of spontaneous reports of thromboembolism following OC use from UK, Sweden, and Denmark. Examines relationship between estrogen dose/progestin type and thromboembolism risk in women using OCs.
Retrospective case-control study of Bulgarian women under 50 years with thromboembolic events. Evaluates OC use and smoking effects on DVT/PE risk. Includes healthy women on OCs with VT outcomes.

Abstract is truncated and appears to be from a review/editorial in NEJM. Discusses historical context and lower-estrogen contraceptives but does not present original research data on healthy women with VT outcomes.
Case-control study of women aged 15-49 years examining VTE risk associated with different COC formulations. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Retrospective case-reference study of women aged 15-44 years examining VTE incidence among COC users. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Matched case-control study of women aged 16-44 years examining VTE risk with different generations of COCs. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Review article discussing pharmacological properties of new progestins. No primary study data on VT outcomes in COC users. Does not meet study design criteria.
Randomized study measuring hemostasis markers (surrogate endpoints) rather than actual VT events. Outcome does not match protocol requirement for VT as outcome.
Review article on APC resistance mechanisms. Not a primary study on COC use and VT. Does not meet population/intervention criteria.
Case-control study of women aged 15-49 years examining VTE risk with low-dose OCs. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Editorial/commentary piece. No primary study data on COC and VT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Methodological paper on evaluating bias in non-randomised studies. Not a primary study on COC and VT. Does not meet any criteria.
Cohort study comparing thromboembolism risk between ethinylestradiol/drospirenone and other OCs. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Nested case-control study examining VTE risk with different COC formulations. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Case-control study of premenopausal women aged 15-49 examining VTE risk in OC users with factor V Leiden. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Methodological paper on detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. Not a primary study on COC and VT. Does not meet any criteria.
Study examining vascular disease risk factors including OC use and venous thromboembolism in women. Meets criteria: women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Prospective cohort study examining PE risk with current and past OC use in women aged 30-55. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome (PE is a form of VT).
Cohort study of women aged 18-46 examining VTE risk with drospirenone-containing COCs at different EE dosages. Meets all criteria: healthy women, COC exposure, VT outcome.
Descriptive epidemiological study reporting hospitalization rates for thromboembolic events. No COC exposure assessment or comparison. Does not meet intervention criteria.
Controlled prospective survey examining thromboembolic disease with anovulant (OC) use. While focused on superficial thrombosis, may contain relevant data. Conservative inclusion per guidelines.
Study on EHPVO (extrahepatic portal vein obstruction), not typical venous thrombosis. States OC use was NOT associated with EHPVO. Different outcome than protocol requires.
Title indicates study of specific OC formulations and VTE requiring hospital admission. Likely meets criteria though abstract is minimal. Conservative inclusion per guidelines.
Prospective cohort study of 58,674 women using drospirenone-containing and other OCs with venous thromboembolism as outcome. Population appears to be healthy women taking COC.
Case-control study examining VT risk in women over 50 using oral contraception. While age group is older, women are taking OC with VT as outcome.
This is a general descriptive article about pill use statistics and market trends. No study design with VT as outcome.
This is a review article discussing pharmacogenetic aspects of OC use and thrombosis risk. Not a primary study with healthy women and VT outcome.
Observational study examining VTE risk in women prescribed CPA/EE (a COC). While some women have acne/hirsutism/PCOS, the study includes all women aged 15-39 and VTE is the outcome.
Population-based case-control study testing oral contraceptives as VTE risk factors. Includes women taking OC with VTE as outcome.
Population-based case-control study of premenopausal women aged 15-49 examining DVT risk with third-generation OCs. Healthy women taking COC with VT as outcome.
Case/non-case study examining diagnostic suspicion and referral bias in OC-VTE studies. Involves women taking OC with VTE as outcome, though methodological focus.
Study of suspected PE cases during COC treatment. Examines COC users with PE (a type of VT) as outcome.
Large prospective study of 17,000 married women aged 25-39 examining VTE in relation to oral contraceptive use. Healthy women taking COC with VT as outcome.
This is a methodological overview comparing RCT and observational study data for adverse effects. Not a study on COC and VT specifically.
Systematic review and meta-analysis summarizing evidence on OC use and VTE risk. Includes 16 cohort and 39 case-control studies of women taking OC with VTE outcome.
Prescription event monitoring study of Yasmin (COC) users with DVT/PE as outcomes. Women taking COC with VT as outcome.
International multicentre case-control study of women aged 20-44 examining VTE risk with combined OCs. Healthy women taking COC with VT as outcome.
Study examining thromboembolic deaths in women of child-bearing age using oral contraceptives. Women taking OC with thromboembolism as outcome.
Population-based cohort and nested case-control study of 540,000 women examining VTE risk with different OC preparations. Women taking COC with VT as outcome.
Case-control study examining VTE risk with third generation OCs in women with and without heritable thrombophilia. Women taking COC with VT as outcome.
Multicenter case-control study examining cardiovascular risk including venous thrombosis in oral contraceptive users. Women taking OC with VT as one of the outcomes.
Randomized trial examining effects of OCs on protein C system and hemostatic variables. The outcome is hemostatic parameters, not venous thrombosis.
Case-control study examining VTE risk factors in pre- and postmenopausal women. Focus is on menopausal hormone therapy, not combined oral contraceptives.

Case-control study examining VTE risk in women using combined oral contraceptives (third vs second generation). Population includes women aged 16-44 years with VTE and matched controls. Directly addresses COC use and VT outcome.
Examines pulmonary embolism (a form of VT) deaths in women under 40 using low-estrogen oral contraceptives. Provides relative risk estimates for PE among OC users.
Systematic review of methodological tools for assessing bias in observational studies. Does not study COC use or VT outcomes in women.
Abstract describes protein labeling techniques and fluorescent dyes for microscopy, completely unrelated to oral contraceptives or venous thrombosis. Appears to be a mismatched abstract.
Review article summarizing various risks and benefits of COCs including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and VT. Does not present original data on healthy women with VT as outcome.
Commentary discussing the 'attrition of susceptibles' hypothesis regarding OCs and VTE. Does not present original study data on healthy women taking COCs with VT outcome.
Case-control study of fatal VTE in women aged 16-39 years. Examines oral contraceptive use as a risk factor. While focused on fatal cases, it includes OC users and VT outcome.
Philosophical/methodological essay about different views of medical science. Does not study COC use or VT outcomes.
Danish case-control study of women 15-44 years with first DVT or PE. Examines OC use, duration, estrogen dose, and progestin type effects on VTE risk. Directly addresses selection criteria.
Abstract describes hepatitis B virus research and immune response mechanisms. Completely unrelated to oral contraceptives or venous thrombosis.
WHO Scientific Group report reviewing existing evidence on hormonal contraceptives and cardiovascular disease. Expert consensus document, not primary research on healthy women with VT outcome.
Studies non-oral contraceptives (injectable depot-medroxyprogesterone acetate and levonorgestrel IUD). Selection criteria specify combined oral contraceptives (COC).
Evaluates diagnostic tests for DVT (D-dimer, ultrasound, etc.). Does not study COC use or risk factors for VT in healthy women.
Meta-analysis of antiplatelet regimens for secondary prevention after TIA/stroke. Not related to COC use or VT in healthy women.
UK database study investigating risk factors for idiopathic VTE in combined oral contraceptive users. Examines age, BMI, smoking, and health status effects. Directly addresses selection criteria.
Reanalysis of Transnational case-control study examining VTE risk in first-time users of second and third generation OCs. Population includes women with VTE and controls.
Retrospective study of thrombosis risk in women using low-estrogen oral contraceptives. Reports relative risk estimates for idiopathic thrombosis cases.
Methodological simulation study on handling attrition in longitudinal data. Not related to COC use or VT outcomes.
Prospective study of PE diagnosis and risk factors. Includes analysis of oral contraceptive use and PE risk, particularly in post-surgical women. Addresses VT outcome in women using OCs.
Nested case-control study comparing VTE risk in women using drospirenone vs levonorgestrel COCs. Population: women 15-44 years without major VT risk factors. Directly addresses selection criteria.

This study does not meet the selection criteria for several reasons: (1) The primary research question focuses on cardiovascular diseases (peripheral atherosclerotic disease and cerebrovascular disease) as risk factors for VTE, not on combined oral contraceptives (COCs). (2) The study population consists of hospitalized patients with various conditions, matched on age, sex, calendar time, and veteran status - not specifically healthy women taking COCs. (3) While 'current estrogen use' is mentioned as one of several independent risk factors in the results, this is not specific to COCs and could include hormone replacement therapy or other estrogen formulations. (4) The study includes both male and female participants (matched on sex), whereas the review requires studies of women only. (5) The study design and objectives do not address the comparison of different COC types or their relative VT risks, which is central to the review objective.
